claims.explanation: Fludroxycortide is a glucocorticoid receptor (NR3C1) agonist, and its selective killing likely reflects glucocorticoid receptor signaling strength and downstream transcriptional output rather than a specific driver mutation. Lines with intact, high NR3C1 expression and glucocorticoid-responsive transcriptional programs (e.g., induction of TSC22D3/NFKBIA and repression of pro-survival NF-kB targets) are expected to be most sensitive, while lines with NR3C1 loss, RAS/MAPK-driven resistance, or mesenchymal/EMT phenotypes are protected. The virtual-cell signature (TSC22D3, NFKBIA, DDIT4 up; IER3, BIRC5 down) and similarity to other GR agonists support an on-target GR mechanism.
